Compute Platforms

CyVerse and KBase power iVirus tools, datasets, and workflows.

Overview

To make virus ecology analyses broadly accessible, iVirus leverages two community platforms: CyVerse and KBase. They provide shared compute, storage, app catalogs, and collaboration features that let researchers run end-to-end workflows without managing their own HPC or devops.

CyVerse

CyVerse democratizes access to advanced computing and data services for life sciences. Researchers can discover apps, launch analyses, and share data via the Discovery Environment and Data Store.

Why it matters here

  • Shared compute and storage for large metagenomics datasets.
  • A place to publish and reuse iVirus datasets.
  • A catalog where iVirus apps and trusted third-party tools run side-by-side.

Citation

This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Award Numbers DBI-0735191, DBI-1265383, and DBI-1743442. URL: www.cyverse.org

KBase

KBase (the DOE Systems Biology Knowledgebase) provides a reproducible, shareable analysis environment with provenance and collaboration features (Narratives) and a curated app catalog.

Why it matters here

  • Reproducible Narratives for end-to-end workflows.
  • Curated apps spanning read processing, assembly, annotation, and downstream analysis.
  • Easy data import from common sources (e.g., NCBI, JGI, SRA).

Citation

Arkin AP, Cottingham RW, Henry CS, Harris NL, Stevens RL, Maslov S, et al. KBase: The United States Department of Energy Systems Biology Knowledgebase. Nature Biotechnology. 2018;36: 566. doi: 10.1038/nbt.4163

Where this fits in iVirus

  • Tools: Many iVirus tools run inside CyVerse or KBase. See Tools & Apps.
  • Workflows & Docs: Protocols and guides reference DE apps and KBase Narratives. See Docs.
  • Data: Community datasets are published in the CyVerse Data Store and referenced from iVirus. See Data.
